verdict.rationale: Codex documents its own MCP client support, letting you add local or remote MCP servers with authentication and inspect their tools. It also documents plugins that 'connect Codex to your team's tools and data'. Slack is a documented surface for starting cloud tasks from channels and threads. However, no evidence shows first-party connectors for Jira or Google Drive, so those depend on whatever MCP servers or plugins a user supplies. missing for 10: documented Jira and Google Drive integrations, evidence that Slack content extends agent context beyond task kickoff, independent hands-on corroboration of workflow-tool connections.

support.subject: As a developer, I can connect the agent to workflow tools like Jira, Slack, and Google Drive to extend its context

citations.quote: Add local or remote MCP servers, authenticate when needed, and inspect the tools available to the current session before Codex uses them.
add plugins to connect Codex to your team's tools and data without leaving the CLI
Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects models to tools and context.
Start work in Codex cloud from GitHub pull requests, GitLab merge requests and issues, Linear issues, or Slack channels and threads.
